This test checks that gopls ignores a go.work file. The go.work file uses
module b, but the view for module a holds only a's go.mod file, and a's
import of b does not resolve. Module b has a path with no dot, so the go
command rejects the import without the network. The rejection is an error
log from go mod tidy.

-- flags --
-mcp
-min_go_command=go1.23
-errors_ok

-- go.work --
go 1.23.0

use (
	./a
	./b
)

-- a/go.mod --
module example.com/a

go 1.23.0

//@mcptool("go_workspace", `{}`, output=workspace)

-- a/a.go --
package a

import _ "workb" //@diag("\"workb\"", re"could not import|not in std|no required module")

-- b/go.mod --
module workb

go 1.23.0

-- b/b.go --
package b

var B int

-- @workspace --
The `$WORKDIR` directory is an ad-hoc Go package, not in a Go module.

The `$WORKDIR/a` directory uses Go modules, with the following main modules:
	$WORKDIR/a/go.mod (module example.com/a)

The `$WORKDIR/b` directory uses Go modules, with the following main modules:
	$WORKDIR/b/go.mod (module workb)
